questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The United Nations was established on which date?
questions.explanation: The UN was officially established on 24 October 1945, when the UN Charter came into force after ratification by the five permanent members and a majority of other signatories. 26 June 1945 is when the Charter was SIGNED in San Francisco. 10 January 1920 is when the League of Nations came into existence. 1 January 1942 is the date of the Declaration by United Nations during WWII.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the UN Security Council:

(i) It has 15 members — 5 permanent and 10 non-permanent.
(ii) Non-permanent members are elected for a term of 2 years.
(iii) Each permanent member has veto power.
(iv) India is a permanent member of the Security Council.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The UNSC has 5 permanent + 10 non-permanent = 15 members (i correct). Non-permanent members serve 2-year terms (ii correct). The P5 (US, UK, France, Russia, China) each have veto power (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — India is NOT a permanent member; it has been a non-permanent member several times and aspires for permanent membership.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The UN General Assembly is called the 'parliament of the world'.
Reason (R): All 193 UN member states have equal representation in the General Assembly, with each having one vote regardless of size or power.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the UNGA is often referred to as the parliament of the world due to its universal membership. Reason (R) is correct — all 193 member states participate equally with one vote each, which is why it resembles a parliament (representative body). The equal representation (R) explains why it's called a parliament (A). Option B is wrong because democratic representation is exactly why it's called a parliament. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following UN organs with their primary functions:

Column I:
(a) General Assembly
(b) Security Council
(c) International Court of Justice
(d) Economic and Social Council

Column II:
(i) Maintenance of international peace and security
(ii) Settlement of legal disputes between states
(iii) Deliberation on international issues by all members
(iv) Coordination of economic and social work of UN agencies

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: General Assembly deliberates on international issues with all members participating (a-iii). Security Council maintains international peace and security (b-i). ICJ settles legal disputes between states (c-ii). ECOSOC coordinates economic and social work of UN agencies (d-iv). Option B swaps GA with SC. Option C mismatches SC with ICJ. Option D incorrectly pairs GA with ECOSOC's role.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following countries are permanent members of the UN Security Council?

(i) United States
(ii) Germany
(iii) France
(iv) China

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The five permanent members (P5) are: United States (i correct), United Kingdom, France (iii correct), Russia, and China (iv correct). Germany (ii) is NOT a permanent member — it is one of the countries seeking permanent membership but does not currently hold it. Options B, C, and D incorrectly include Germany.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The headquarters of the United Nations is located in:
questions.explanation: The main UN headquarters is in New York City, USA. Geneva houses the UN Office at Geneva (UNOG) and many specialized agencies but is not the main HQ. Vienna has the UN Office at Vienna (UNOV). The Hague houses the International Court of Justice. All are important UN locations but New York is the primary headquarters.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the International Court of Justice (ICJ):

(i) It is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.
(ii) It is located at The Hague, Netherlands.
(iii) It has 15 judges elected for 9-year terms.
(iv) Its decisions are binding only if both parties agree to submit to its jurisdiction.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct. ICJ is the principal judicial organ of the UN (i). It's located at the Peace Palace in The Hague (ii). It has 15 judges serving 9-year terms, with 5 elected every 3 years (iii). Its jurisdiction in contentious cases requires consent of the states concerned (iv).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The veto power allows any single permanent member to block a Security Council resolution.
Reason (R): The veto was designed to prevent the UN from taking action against the interests of any major power, ensuring their continued participation.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — any P5 member can veto (block) a substantive UNSC resolution with a negative vote. Reason (R) is correct — the veto was designed at the 1945 San Francisco Conference to keep major powers engaged, unlike the League of Nations which the US never joined. The rationale in (R) explains why the veto exists (A). Option B is wrong because (R) is the historical rationale. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The UN agency responsible for international civil aviation safety and regulations is:
questions.explanation: ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organization) is the UN specialized agency for international aviation standards and regulations, headquartered in Montreal. IATA is an industry trade association (not a UN body). FAA is the US domestic aviation regulator. UNESCO deals with education, science, and culture — not aviation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following UN agencies with their headquarters:

Column I:
(a) WHO
(b) UNESCO
(c) UNICEF
(d) FAO

Column II:
(i) New York
(ii) Paris
(iii) Geneva
(iv) Rome

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: WHO headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland (a-iii). UNESCO is headquartered in Paris, France (b-ii). UNICEF is headquartered in New York, USA (c-i). FAO is headquartered in Rome, Italy (d-iv). Option B swaps WHO with UNESCO. Option C mismatches UNESCO with FAO. Option D incorrectly places WHO in New York.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about UNICEF:

(i) It stands for United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund.
(ii) It was created in 1946 to provide emergency food and healthcare to children in post-war countries.
(iii) It was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965.
(iv) It works exclusively in African countries.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: UNICEF originally stood for United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund (i correct). It was created in 1946 for post-war child welfare (ii correct). It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1965 (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — UNICEF operates in over 190 countries worldwide, not exclusively in Africa.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The current number of member states in the United Nations is:
questions.explanation: The UN has 193 member states (as of 2024, South Sudan being the latest to join in 2011). 192 was the count before South Sudan joined. 195 includes non-member observer states (Vatican City and Palestine). 189 is an outdated figure.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are principal organs of the United Nations?

(i) General Assembly
(ii) Security Council
(iii) World Health Organization
(iv) Trusteeship Council

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The six principal organs of the UN are: General Assembly (i correct), Security Council (ii correct), Economic and Social Council, Trusteeship Council (iv correct — though now inactive), International Court of Justice, and Secretariat. WHO (iii) is a SPECIALIZED AGENCY, not a principal organ. Options B, C, and D incorrectly include WHO as a principal organ.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The UN Secretary-General is often described as the 'world's diplomat'.
Reason (R): The Secretary-General serves as the chief administrative officer of the UN and can bring to the Security Council's attention any matter that may threaten international peace.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Secretary-General is often called the world's top diplomat. Reason (R) is correct — as chief admin officer with Article 99 powers to alert the Security Council, the SG plays a key diplomatic role. The administrative and diplomatic powers in (R) explain the title in (A). Option B is wrong because (R) explains the diplomatic role. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly in which year?
questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted on 10 December 1948 (celebrated as Human Rights Day). 1945 was the year the UN was founded (Charter signed). 1950 is incorrect. 1966 is when the two International Covenants (ICCPR and ICESCR) were adopted, not the UDHR.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the World Health Organization (WHO):

(i) It is a specialized agency of the United Nations.
(ii) Its headquarters is in Geneva, Switzerland.
(iii) It was established in 1948.
(iv) Its primary role is to regulate international trade.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: WHO is a UN specialized agency (i correct). Its HQ is in Geneva (ii correct). It was established on 7 April 1948 (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — WHO's role is international public health, NOT trade regulation. Trade regulation is the domain of the WTO.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following UN programmes/agencies with their areas of work:

Column I:
(a) UNDP
(b) UNHCR
(c) WFP
(d) ILO

Column II:
(i) Labour rights and employment
(ii) Development and poverty reduction
(iii) Food assistance in emergencies
(iv) Protection of refugees

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: UNDP works on development and poverty reduction (a-ii). UNHCR (UN High Commissioner for Refugees) protects refugees (b-iv). WFP (World Food Programme) provides food assistance (c-iii). ILO (International Labour Organization) deals with labour rights (d-i). Option B swaps UNDP with UNHCR. Option C mismatches UNHCR with WFP. Option D incorrectly pairs UNDP with labour.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The United Nations Charter was signed at which conference?
questions.explanation: The UN Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 at the United Nations Conference on International Organization in San Francisco. Yalta discussed post-war order but didn't sign the Charter. Bretton Woods established the IMF and World Bank. Dumbarton Oaks proposed the structure of the UN but the Charter was finalized and signed at San Francisco.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The UN Security Council requires a minimum of __________ affirmative votes out of 15 for a substantive resolution to pass, including no veto from any permanent member.
questions.explanation: A substantive UNSC resolution requires at least 9 affirmative votes (out of 15) and no negative vote (veto) from any of the 5 permanent members. 10 is too high. 8 is below the required threshold. 7 is a simple majority but not sufficient for the UNSC.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about UNESCO:

(i) It stands for United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization.
(ii) Its headquarters is in Paris, France.
(iii) It designates World Heritage Sites.
(iv) It was established in 1970.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: UNESCO stands for United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (i correct). Its HQ is in Paris (ii correct). It designates UNESCO World Heritage Sites (iii correct). Statement (iv) is incorrect — UNESCO was established in 1945 (constitution signed) and came into force in November 1946, NOT 1970.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The UN Trusteeship Council suspended its operations in 1994.
Reason (R): All Trust Territories had achieved self-governance or independence by then, fulfilling the Council's mandate.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the Trusteeship Council suspended operations on 1 November 1994. Reason (R) is correct — the last Trust Territory (Palau) became independent in 1994, leaving no territories under trusteeship. Since all territories achieved independence (R), the Council had no work left (A). Option B is wrong because (R) is the direct cause. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are specialized agencies of the United Nations?

(i) International Monetary Fund (IMF)
(ii) World Bank
(iii) World Trade Organization (WTO)
(iv) International Labour Organization (ILO)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: IMF (i), World Bank (ii), and ILO (iv) are UN specialized agencies linked through formal agreements. WTO (iii) is NOT a UN specialized agency — it is an independent intergovernmental organization. While WTO cooperates with the UN system, it has no formal specialized agency relationship. Options B and D incorrectly include WTO.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The term of the UN Secretary-General is:
questions.explanation: The UN Secretary-General serves a 5-year term, which can be renewed (most have served two terms). 4 years is incorrect. 6 years non-renewable is not the correct duration or condition. 7 years is the term for some other international positions but not the UN SG.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following UN Secretaries-General with their countries of origin:

Column I:
(a) Kofi Annan
(b) Ban Ki-moon
(c) António Guterres
(d) Boutros Boutros-Ghali

Column II:
(i) South Korea
(ii) Portugal
(iii) Ghana
(iv) Egypt

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Kofi Annan was from Ghana (a-iii). Ban Ki-moon from South Korea (b-i). António Guterres from Portugal (c-ii). Boutros Boutros-Ghali from Egypt (d-iv). Option B swaps Annan with Ban Ki-moon. Option C mismatches Ban Ki-moon with Guterres. Option D incorrectly pairs Annan with Egypt.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the UN General Assembly:

(i) It meets in regular annual sessions beginning in September.
(ii) Decisions on important questions require a two-thirds majority.
(iii) It can override the Security Council's veto.
(iv) It elects non-permanent members of the Security Council.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The GA meets annually starting in September (i correct). Important decisions need two-thirds majority (ii correct). It elects the 10 non-permanent UNSC members (iv correct). Statement (iii) is incorrect — the GA CANNOT override the Security Council's veto; the veto is absolute on substantive matters (though the 'Uniting for Peace' resolution allows the GA to make recommendations when the SC is deadlocked).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: IAEA is headquartered in Vienna, Austria. Geneva hosts WHO, WTO, and other agencies. New York has the main UN headquarters. Brussels is the EU headquarters. Vienna is an important UN hub hosting IAEA, UNIDO, and UNODC.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India has been elected as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council multiple times.
Reason (R): Non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly based on equitable geographical distribution for 2-year terms.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — India has been a non-permanent UNSC member 8 times (most recently 2021-22). Reason (R) is correct — the election process uses geographical distribution for 2-year terms. However, (R) doesn't explain WHY India was elected multiple times — it only describes the general election mechanism. India's repeated election is due to its diplomatic standing and regional support, not simply the existence of the election process. Option A is wrong because (R) describes the process, not India's specific success. Option C is wrong because (R) is factually correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following correctly describes the 'veto power' in the UN Security Council?

(i) Only the 5 permanent members possess veto power.
(ii) A single veto can block any substantive resolution.
(iii) The veto cannot be used on procedural matters.
(iv) The veto power has never been used since 1945.

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Only P5 members have veto power (i correct). One veto blocks a resolution (ii correct). Veto applies only to substantive matters, not procedural ones (iii correct). Statement (iv) is INCORRECT — the veto has been used hundreds of times since 1945 by various permanent members, particularly during the Cold War.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The World Food Programme (WFP), which won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020, is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: WFP is headquartered in Rome, Italy (along with FAO and IFAD). Geneva hosts WHO and others. New York has the main UN HQ. Nairobi has UNEP and UN-Habitat but not WFP. WFP won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020 for its efforts to combat hunger.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC):

(i) It has 54 members elected for 3-year terms.
(ii) It coordinates the work of UN specialized agencies.
(iii) It can make binding decisions on member states.
(iv) It promotes international economic and social cooperation.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: ECOSOC has 54 members with 3-year terms (i correct). It coordinates UN specialized agencies (ii correct). It promotes economic and social cooperation (iv correct). Statement (iii) is incorrect — ECOSOC can only make RECOMMENDATIONS, not binding decisions. Only the Security Council can make binding decisions under Chapter VII.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the annual __________ which ranks countries by life expectancy, education, and per capita income.
questions.explanation: UNDP publishes the Human Development Report containing the Human Development Index (HDI) which measures life expectancy, education, and income. The World Development Report is by the World Bank. The Global Competitiveness Report is by the World Economic Forum. The World Happiness Report is supported by the UN but not published by UNDP specifically.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following international days with the UN agency that promotes them:

Column I:
(a) World Health Day (7 April)
(b) World Food Day (16 October)
(c) International Literacy Day (8 September)
(d) World Environment Day (5 June)

Column II:
(i) UNEP
(ii) WHO
(iii) FAO
(iv) UNESCO

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: World Health Day is promoted by WHO (a-ii). World Food Day by FAO (b-iii). International Literacy Day by UNESCO (c-iv). World Environment Day by UNEP (d-i). Option B swaps WHO with FAO. Option C mismatches Food Day with UNESCO. Option D incorrectly pairs Health Day with UNEP.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The UN peacekeeping forces are popularly known as:
questions.explanation: UN peacekeepers are called 'Blue Helmets' because of their distinctive blue helmets and berets. 'Green Berets' are US Army Special Forces. 'Red Cross' is the international humanitarian organization (ICRC). 'White Helmets' refers to Syrian Civil Defence volunteers. Only Blue Helmets identifies UN peacekeepers.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India and the United Nations:

(i) India was a founding member of the United Nations in 1945.
(ii) India has contributed the largest number of troops to UN peacekeeping operations.
(iii) India is a permanent member of the Security Council.
(iv) India has been elected to the UNSC as a non-permanent member 8 times.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: India was a founding UN member (i correct). India is among the largest contributors to UN peacekeeping (ii correct). India has served on the UNSC 8 times as a non-permanent member (iv correct). Statement (iii) is incorrect — India is NOT a permanent member of the Security Council; it has been campaigning for permanent membership.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is unique among UN agencies because:
options: It has a tripartite structure with representatives from governments, employers, and workers
It only admits developed countries as members
It can enforce its decisions militarily
questions.correctAnswer: It has a tripartite structure with representatives from governments, employers, and workers
questions.explanation: ILO is unique for its tripartite governance — each member state sends delegates representing government, employers, AND workers. No other UN agency has this three-party structure. It does not restrict membership to developed countries. It has no military enforcement power. It operates globally, not just in Europe.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows the number of times the veto was used by P5 members (approximate totals through 2023):

| Country | Approximate Vetoes |
|---------|-------------------|
| Russia/USSR | 120 |
| USA | 82 |
| UK | 29 |
| France | 16 |
| China | 17 |

Which country has used the veto the LEAST number of times?
questions.explanation: France has used approximately 16 vetoes — the lowest among the P5. China has used about 17 (slightly more). UK has used 29. USA has used 82. Russia/USSR leads with approximately 120. France at 16 is the least frequent user of the veto power.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The United Nations replaced the League of Nations as the primary international organization for maintaining peace.
Reason (R): The League of Nations failed to prevent World War II due to the absence of major powers and lack of enforcement mechanisms.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion (A) is correct — the UN replaced the League of Nations in 1945. Reason (R) is correct — the League failed because the US never joined, other powers withdrew, and it lacked enforcement power. The League's failures (R) directly led to the creation of the UN as a stronger replacement (A). Option B is wrong because (R) is the direct cause of the replacement. Option C is wrong because (R) is correct. Option D is wrong because (A) is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are functions of the UN Security Council?

(i) Recommending admission of new members to the General Assembly
(ii) Imposing economic sanctions on countries
(iii) Authorizing military action to restore peace
(iv) Electing judges of the ICJ (jointly with GA)

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: All are UNSC functions. It recommends new members for GA approval (i correct). It can impose sanctions under Chapter VII (ii correct). It can authorize military force (iii correct). It participates in electing ICJ judges jointly with the GA (iv correct). All four are established UNSC powers.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following data shows India's contributions to UN peacekeeping:

| Decade | Personnel Contributed (approx.) |
|--------|-------------------------------|
| 1950s-60s | 10,000 |
| 1970s-80s | 25,000 |
| 1990s-2000s | 80,000 |
| 2010s-2020s | 60,000 |

In which period was India's contribution the highest?
questions.explanation: India's contribution peaked at approximately 80,000 personnel during the 1990s-2000s period. The 2010s-2020s saw a slight decrease to 60,000. The 1970s-80s contributed 25,000. The 1950s-60s was the initial period with 10,000. The 1990s-2000s clearly had the highest numbers.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Sustainable Development Goals' (SDGs) adopted by the UN in 2015 contain how many goals to be achieved by 2030?
questions.explanation: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development includes 17 SDGs covering poverty, hunger, health, education, equality, environment, and more. 15 is the number of MDGs' target year (2015). 12 and 20 are incorrect numbers. The SDGs replaced the 8 Millennium Development Goals (MDGs).
